:::{#exr-centered-data-rank-practice}
#### Finding how large the rank of centered data can be

Centering a data [matrix](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix) subtracts the [mean](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd#def-mean) row from every row,
and @thm-centered-data-rank shows how large the [rank](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-rank) of the result can be.
Suppose that $\mX$ holds $3$ observations of $4$ features, as a $3 \times 4$ matrix,
and $\mX_c$ is its centered version.

Find the number that, by @thm-centered-data-rank, $\rankf{\mX_c}$ cannot exceed.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Compare the number from @thm-centered-data-rank with the one from @cor-rank-bound.

:::
